archetype.name: Playoff Team (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A Jokić-and-Murray offense that scores efficiently enough to win most nights, paired with a below-average defense that caps how far the margin can stretch.

report.headline: The usual Denver: elite starters, a leaky middle, and a soft wing spot
report.take:
Denver is 5-3 on a modest +2.1 Net Rtg, 17th in the league, and the record matches the margin: W vs Pt Diff is 0, and the differential implies 5 wins. There's no luck to strip out. The shape is familiar from recent seasons, a top-ten offense (117.5 ORtg, 7th) on top of a defense in the bottom half (115.4 DRtg, 19th). The site's 17th-place ranking is harsher than the five-year run of 48 to 57 wins suggests, because the margin hasn't yet matched those teams.

The offense runs through the same two players. Nikola Jokić is 2nd on the center tab with a 7.4 BPM, and Jamal Murray is 5th among point guards, scoring at a 64.4 TS %. Denver doesn't hunt threes (38.2 3PA Rate, 25th) but converts what it takes: eFG % 55.4 ranks 4th and FT Rate 31.5 ranks 6th. The starting backcourt is the story of the minutes. Murray is +17.4 On-Off and Christian Braun +19.7, while Tyus Jones, the main backup guard, sits at -20.9. Lineups with the stars on the floor have won comfortably, and the bench minutes have given much of it back.

The numbers hide a slide from last year's peak. The 2025-26 team led the league in ORtg at 122.6 and made 39.6% of its threes. This one is at 36.0%, and the offensive rating has come down with it. The defense has the same problem it had then (Def Rank 21 last season, 19 now), and it has gotten worse at the rim. Opponents shoot 68.4% there (23rd) and get there on 32.4% of their shots (22nd). The wing spot is the clearest hole. Small forwards have scored 29.63 a game against Denver, the most in the league, and the wings grade D-. DeMar DeRozan has a -4.5 BPM and a -17.1 On-Off on 51.8 TS %.

The last five games are encouraging. Denver went 4-1 at +8.6 a game and allowed 108 a game, more than five points better than its season average. The opponents were mostly middling to weak, though, and the two worst nights of the season came against OKC and Golden State. This looks like a 50-win team, not a contender, unless the three-point shooting returns to last year's level or the wing minutes get better.

strengths.title: Jokić and Murray carry elite efficiency
strengths.body: Jokić ranks 2nd at center and Murray 5th at point guard, and together they have the team shooting a 59.9 TS %, 4th in the league. The efficiency comes from shot quality and free throws rather than three-point volume, which tends to hold up over a season. This core has produced a top-six offense in each of the last five years.

strengths.title: Starting guards swing the net rating
strengths.body: Braun's +19.7 and Murray's +17.4 On-Off are the biggest on the roster. Braun's backcourt has held shooting guards to the fewest points in the league. The A- backcourt grade is earned at both ends, not just carried by Murray's scoring.

strengths.title: Low turnovers, frequent free throws
strengths.body: A 13.0 TOV % (8th) and a 31.5 FT Rate (6th) give Denver possessions other teams don't get. Ball security has been a hallmark of this offense for years, though last season's 11.5 was cleaner still.

concerns.title: Wings and forwards are getting torched
concerns.body: Small forwards score 29.63 a game against Denver (30th) and power forwards 26.88 (28th). Small forwards take a share of the points against Denver well above the league norm. The D- wing group, led by DeRozan's -17.1 On-Off, gives up as much at that end as it fails to provide at the other. Unless the minutes shift toward the forwards with positive On-Off numbers, this looks structural rather than noise.

concerns.title: Soft at the rim and on the glass
concerns.body: Opponents get to the rim often and finish there at 68.4% (23rd). Denver also secures only 71.2% of defensive rebounds, 22nd and below the 75.3% of last season. That combination explains most of a DRtg sitting two points worse than the league average. The rebounding should improve toward its usual level, but the rim protection has been middling for years.

concerns.title: Thin bench, long day-to-day list
concerns.body: Jokić, Murray, Braun, Gordon, DeRozan and Johnson are all listed day-to-day. Backup point guards Tyus Jones (-20.9) and Ryan Nembhard (-22.7) have been badly outscored in their minutes. If the starters miss time or play shorter minutes, the margin can disappear quickly.

trend.note: Denver opened 3-2 while being outscored in October, including a 20-point home loss to Golden State. It has since gone 4-1 at +8.6 a game, mostly on defense, though the stretch came against mid-tier and weaker teams.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, opening against two top-eight teams
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at Houston (7-3, 6th on the site, +9.3 Net Rtg) and at Memphis (6-3, 8th). Both are better teams than Denver by margin, and both attack its weak spots. Houston's frontcourt grades A+ and its wings A-, and it grabs 31.5% of its own misses. Memphis leads the league in RPG. A Denver team ranked 22nd in DRB % could lose both games on second chances.

The back half is kinder. Denver has already beaten New Orleans twice, and the Pelicans allow 70.7% at the rim (26th), which suits Jokić. Phoenix sits 25th on the site and is last in DRB %. Splitting the first two and winning the last two would make it a good week, and anything less than 2-2 would raise questions about the recent defensive surge.

keyMatchups.title: Defensive glass against Houston and Memphis
keyMatchups.body: Denver's 71.2 DRB % ranks 22nd. Houston's 31.5 ORB % ranks 6th, and Memphis's 53.3 REB % ranks 2nd. Extra possessions are how these two road games get away from Denver, so this is the number to watch.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's wings against Denver's weakest spot
keyMatchups.body: Houston's wings grade A-, and Denver has given up more points to small forwards than any defense in the league. Houston also holds opponents to 31.6% from three (2nd), which could keep Denver's shooting slump going. This is the toughest game of the week.

keyMatchups.title: Murray and Jokić against Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix gives up 35.75 a game to point guards (30th) and 25 to centers (29th). That lines up directly with Denver's two stars. The Suns also rank 30th in DRB %, so Jokić should own the glass in the home finale.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the 108-a-game defense of the last five holds up against Houston's and Memphis's size.

restOfSeason.body:
The record is honest, with no close-game luck to give back, and the current rate projects to about 51 wins. The offense should improve somewhat: this core has shot 37% or better from three in each of the last four seasons, and 36.0% looks more like a slow start than a new level. The defense is more likely to stay where it is, as it has finished in the bottom half in most recent years. The recent drop in points allowed probably reflects the schedule more than a real change. Final wins of 48 to 54 is the reasonable range, with an ORtg around 117 to 121 and a DRtg around 114 to 117.

The ceiling depends on health and the wing spot. The starters have been dominant and the bench has been badly outscored, so the long day-to-day list is the biggest downside risk. Any lasting improvement at small forward would raise the ceiling more than any other change.

confidence.note: Eight games, a soft recent schedule, and a long day-to-day list.
